nodes.label: Amber, Navy and Slate-Blue Brand Palette
nodes.author: RealFaviconGenerator
nodes.norm_label: amber, navy and slate-blue brand palette

nodes.label: Feedback model (criticisms & suggestions)
nodes.rationale: Anonymous-allowed from /contact-us; name optional because there is no phone/email to follow up on, and it is not mixed into Leads.

nodes.label: Lead model (lead submissions)
nodes.rationale: Visitors interact via Lead forms expecting a name and a way to reply; metadata JSON holds e.g. courseSlug/tier for enroll leads, status defaults NEW.

nodes.label: Leads dashboard as notification surface
nodes.rationale: Landing page of /admin shows recent leads with a prominent new count; there is no email notification pipeline, so the dashboard itself is the notification surface.

nodes.label: Lead-focused analytics event plan
nodes.rationale: Track moments mapping to actual goals (leads) rather than vanity events: enroll, class seat, sponsor, school, job, contact, feedback, video_play, download_click, language_switch — with fa/en as a property to validate whether English content converts.

nodes.label: Lead-capture business model (no payments)
nodes.rationale: All monetization-adjacent flows are lead capture (enroll, class-seat, sponsor, school, job, contact); they route to leads stored in the database and visible in the admin panel — no email notification pipeline.

nodes.label: Balad icon color palette (purple, amber, orange, white)
nodes.norm_label: balad icon color palette (purple, amber, orange, white)

nodes.label: Neshan mapping / navigation service brand identity
nodes.norm_label: neshan mapping / navigation service brand identity

nodes.label: Red and navy-blue interlocking swooshes forming the outer mark
nodes.norm_label: red and navy-blue interlocking swooshes forming the outer mark

nodes.label: Red-and-White Pennant Motif
nodes.rationale: A small red-and-white flag/pennant above the robot head adds a national/cultural accent consistent with the Persian-named project, providing a splash of accent color against the otherwise gold/navy design.

nodes.label: Gold and Navy Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Dominant gold/amber (#E8A81C-like) against dark navy (#1B2A3A-like) with cream highlights gives strong figure-ground contrast for legibility at icon scale and a tech-meets-premium brand feel.

nodes.label: Robot Mascot Head
nodes.rationale: A friendly, approachable robot face (two large round gold eyes, side panels/'ears', and a mouth/visor panel) is chosen as the app's character to make a technical tool feel personable and memorable.

nodes.label: Shield / Badge Frame
nodes.rationale: A gold shield/badge silhouette frames the robot, conveying trust, protection, and identity — a common app-emblem convention that reads well in a circular/squircle icon crop.

nodes.label: Web App Manifest Icon (512×512)
nodes.rationale: Serves as the installable PWA icon; a bold, flat-vector, high-contrast robot mascot is used so the app stays recognizable at small sizes on home screens and launch screens.

nodes.label: iOS Apple Touch App Icon Role
nodes.norm_label: ios apple touch app icon role

nodes.label: Red-White-Red Banner Motif on Robot Head
nodes.norm_label: red-white-red banner motif on robot head

nodes.label: Robot Face with Circular Lens Eyes
nodes.norm_label: robot face with circular lens eyes

nodes.label: Pishnam Robot Mascot Apple Touch Icon
nodes.norm_label: pishnam robot mascot apple touch icon

nodes.label: Typography (Vazirmatn / Inter)
nodes.rationale: Vazirmatn variable font for Persian; Inter or Vazirmatn for English; Persian needs slightly larger base size (16-18px) than Latin.

nodes.label: Performance targets (Lighthouse ≥ 90 mobile, lazy Aparat embeds)
nodes.norm_label: performance targets (lighthouse ≥ 90 mobile, lazy aparat embeds)
nodes.rationale: Mobile-first testing at ~360-414px; self-hosted Vazirmatn via next/font/local; Aparat embeds lazy-loaded because the current WP site loads them eagerly.

nodes.label: Rendering strategy per page type (SSG/ISR/SSR)
nodes.rationale: Static marketing pages SSG; courses/videos/downloads ISR every few hours; blog ISR ~10-30 min; admin SSR behind auth; forms client component + server action/API route.

nodes.label: Performance as SEO (Core Web Vitals)
nodes.rationale: Core Web Vitals count toward ranking, reinforcing the Lighthouse ≥ 90 mobile and lazy-loaded embed targets.

nodes.label: Camera Pictogram Outline with Lens and Dot
nodes.norm_label: camera pictogram outline with lens and dot

nodes.label: AdminUser model (owner/editor roles)
nodes.community_name: Docs: Database Schema / Docs: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Custom admin, not public accounts; disabledAt lets an owner suspend an account; an owner cannot disable themselves or the last enabled owner.

nodes.label: Admin auth (NextAuth Credentials; owner/editor roles)
nodes.community_name: Docs: Database Schema / Docs: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Single AdminUser table, no public accounts; NextAuth recommended over hand-rolling session security; /admin/** gated in the segment root layout, redirecting to /admin/login.

nodes.label: NextAuth.js v5 (Credentials provider)
nodes.community_name: Docs: Database Schema / Docs: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Admin-only; no public accounts.

nodes.label: Admin explicitly out of scope for v1
nodes.community_name: Docs: Admin Panel / Docs: Analytics & i18n
nodes.norm_label: admin explicitly out of scope for v1
nodes.rationale: No multi-level approvals, no public accounts, no analytics dashboards inside admin (use Umami directly), no payment/order management.

nodes.label: Umami self-hosted analytics
nodes.community_name: Docs: Admin Panel / Docs: Analytics & i18n
nodes.rationale: Privacy-friendly and cookie-consent-free by design; self-hosted or Cloud both work, self-hosted keeps everything in the existing infra story.

nodes.label: Next.js 16 (App Router)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed, not open for reconsideration; covers both marketing site and admin in one app/repo and builds on the solo developer's existing Next.js experience.

nodes.label: Framework decision: Next.js 16 App Router (CONFIRMED)
nodes.rationale: Covers marketing site and admin in one app/repo (single-repo requirement), builds on existing Next.js experience (most important for a solo project), and gives SSR/SSG/ISR plus strong SEO defaults.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md — Next.js 16 agent rules
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes; read the relevant guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is written and re-added by next dev (see node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js), so removing it from a diff only recreates the uncommitted change.

nodes.label: DownloadResource model (flat categories)
nodes.rationale: Fully public, no gating; source HOSTED vs EXTERNAL changes how fileUrl is validated; cadTool replaces former separate SolidWorks/Altium categories.

nodes.label: Bilingual SEO scope and WP URL redirects
nodes.norm_label: bilingual seo scope and wp url redirects
nodes.rationale: No local-SEO work and no WordPress rankings to preserve, but redirect old WP URLs where a clear 1:1 mapping exists as a low-cost safety net against dead backlinks.

nodes.label: SEO content guidelines (Persian search intent)
nodes.rationale: English pages are not literal translations — write for an English-searching audience; one h1 per page and descriptive alt text (e.g. name the team, event, year, and result, not IMG_2312).

nodes.label: sitemap.xml and robots.txt
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated app/sitemap.ts covering both locales; robots.txt allows public routes but disallows /admin/** and API routes.

nodes.rationale: Strict mode worth the upfront friction solo, since it catches mistakes that would otherwise surface as production bugs with no one else to catch them.

nodes.label: Tiptap rich text editor

nodes.norm_label: doc index (docs/ as source of truth)

nodes.label: Documentation habits (docs/ as source of truth)
nodes.norm_label: documentation habits (docs/ as source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Update docs alongside code changes, especially 04-database-schema.md whenever schema.prisma changes; inline comments reserved for why, not what.

nodes.label: README.md — Pishnam project overview
nodes.rationale: Full product/technical spec lives in docs/ as the source of truth; keep it in sync with prisma/schema.prisma and this README as things change.

nodes.label: Audience entry points concept
nodes.rationale: Each audience should have a clear, short path from the homepage, not buried in a mega-menu.

nodes.label: Five target audiences
nodes.rationale: Parents, students, prospective sponsors, schools/institutions, and general public/press — all need distinct entry points on the site, not one generic homepage.

nodes.label: Brand assets / placeholder logo rule
nodes.rationale: Existing robot-badge logo kept as-is; final production file supplied later, so use a simple placeholder mark and do not design a new logo.

nodes.label: Dual tone-of-voice registers
nodes.rationale: Credible/technical register for courses, results, sponsors, schools; playful/kid-friendly for entry-level courses, homepage hero, simple blog posts. Never mix registers within a single page.

nodes.label: Content types requiring admin CRUD
nodes.rationale: Any new content type must be added to both 04-database-schema.md and 06-admin-panel.md — don't hardcode content that should be editable.

nodes.label: Accessibility baseline (WCAG AA)
nodes.rationale: Verify contrast in both modes independently, keyboard-navigable interactive elements, aria-live form errors (not color alone), and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Logo-derived brand color palette
nodes.rationale: Gold #E6A817, navy #18222D, steel blue #3B5E82, off-white #F2F2F0, red #E5001A — confirmed from the logo, replacing earlier placeholder hex values. Brand anchors stay identical in light and dark mode.

nodes.label: Key components to build (SiteHeader, AudienceEntryCard, LeadCaptureForm, ...)
nodes.norm_label: key components to build (siteheader, audienceentrycard, leadcaptureform, ...)

nodes.label: Competition → League → PosterCategory → CompetitionPoster hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Replaces flat POSTERS DownloadResource rows so admins manage categories per competition/league and the public page groups accordingly.

nodes.label: ContactSettings singleton
nodes.rationale: One row (id='default'), not a list of locations; phones is String[]; mapEmbedUrl stores only a canonical Google Maps embed URL; missing fields are omitted on /contact-us rather than showing placeholder copy.

nodes.label: Course + CourseTranslation models
nodes.rationale: Rich text uses a per-locale translation table with @@unique([courseId, locale]) so adding a locale later doesn't require a parent-table migration.

nodes.label: DatasheetPart two-level tree + media children
nodes.rationale: A part is a stand-alone module or a family with variant children (nesting capped at two levels); children hold documents, videos, images, and code samples.

nodes.label: HeroSlide collection
nodes.rationale: A table rather than columns on a settings singleton because 'how many photos does the hero show?' is a question a table answers; alt text lives on the slide because only the uploader can describe it; zero rows renders the hero fallback.

nodes.label: HomepageStats singleton
nodes.rationale: Manual marketing numbers driving the hero count-up strip, not derived from Lead or Achievement rows; strip hidden until the row is saved.

nodes.label: Prisma schema (draft) — PostgreSQL data model
nodes.rationale: Content volume is small (dozens per type); no separate search engine needed, no payments, no user progress-tracking. Use prisma migrate from day one, committed to the repo.

nodes.label: SoftwareProduct + SoftwareRelease models
nodes.rationale: One product per app/plugin with a picture and own page; one release row per platform/version — the one download category not a flat DownloadResource list because a single row can't represent one product with several files.

nodes.label: Postgres tsvector search plan
nodes.rationale: Use tsvector columns on CourseTranslation, ArticleTranslation, and Faq rather than adding a new search service.

nodes.label: Server Components + Server Actions data fetching
nodes.norm_label: server components + server actions data fetching
nodes.rationale: Server Components fetch directly via Prisma (no internal API layer for the frontend); forms submit to Server Actions writing to Lead with no email notification; admin uses Server Actions/Components behind session checks. Keeps business logic reachable as a future mobile API surface.

nodes.label: Admin CRUD surfaces per content type
nodes.norm_label: admin crud surfaces per content type
nodes.rationale: One section per schema model, including courses, products/tags, class sessions, achievements/tags, licenses, team, FAQs, videos, downloads hierarchy, software, datasheets, articles, jobs, leads, feedback, contact, homepage stats.

nodes.label: Reusable AdminForm / DataTable CRUD pattern (Tiptap)
nodes.rationale: One config-driven AdminForm instead of a bespoke form per type; side-by-side FA/EN fields reduce the chance of shipping half-translated content; every image upload goes through the 05 upload security checklist.

nodes.label: generateMetadata / Next.js Metadata API
nodes.rationale: Title template %s | پیشنام / %s | Pishnam, unique 120-160 char descriptions, alternates.languages hreflang with x-default to Persian, OG + Twitter cards for shareable achievements and articles.

nodes.label: URL structure (no /fa prefix, /en prefix)
nodes.rationale: Persian is primary so pishnam.com/ has no /fa prefix; keep slugs stable once published because changing them loses accumulated ranking.

nodes.label: Content parity workflow (FA/EN fields together)
nodes.rationale: Show FA and EN fields together so nothing ships half-translated; a missing-translation indicator in the admin list view is an optional nice-to-have, not required for v1.

nodes.label: next-intl routing + message management
nodes.rationale: Full bilingual parity, not an English landing page: handles locale-prefixed routing, hreflang, RTL/LTR switching; static UI strings in messages/fa.json and messages/en.json.

nodes.label: SSH tunnel to production Postgres (npm run db:tunnel)
nodes.norm_label: ssh tunnel to production postgres (npm run db:tunnel)
nodes.rationale: Production Postgres is published on the server's loopback only (127.0.0.1:5433 -> localhost:5434), never 0.0.0.0, so a tunnel is the only route in; infra/db-tunnel.sh sets ExitOnForwardFailure and pre-checks the port because picking pishtalk's local port would silently leave Prisma pointed at the wrong DB.

nodes.label: Docker Compose full stack (Postgres, migrator, web, nginx)
nodes.norm_label: docker compose full stack (postgres, migrator, web, nginx)
nodes.rationale: The migrator is a one-off job that applies pending Prisma migrations then bootstraps the first admin, both idempotent; web waits for it to exit 0.

nodes.label: messages/{fa,en}.json — UI strings only
nodes.rationale: Content always lives in the database, never in message files, so it stays admin-editable.

nodes.label: next-intl routing and i18n
nodes.rationale: / = Persian (default, RTL), /en/... = English (LTR).

nodes.label: Shared VPS production host (pishtalk, iranopen-insitu)
nodes.rationale: Nothing in this compose project may bind :80 (our nginx takes :8081 as host default_server), and images are never pulled on the server — ~1 in 5 TLS handshakes to ghcr.io complete, and 3.8 GB RAM leaves no headroom for next build, so CI builds and streams images over SSH.

nodes.label: Local-disk uploads Docker volume
nodes.rationale: Files must live in a named Docker volume, never the app's writable container layer, or they'd be lost on every redeploy.

nodes.label: Definition of done (AI instructions)
nodes.rationale: Works in fa and en, responsive from ~360px, no console errors, passes lint + typecheck, content admin-editable, and metadata per 07-seo-guidelines.md.

nodes.label: Non-negotiable constraints for AI agents
nodes.rationale: Next.js 16 confirmed; no payments/LMS; single repo; bilingual from day one; light and dark mode; locked brand colors; local-disk media; full upload checklist on every upload; keep logo/brand name; ask on product decisions. Do not violate without explicit human sign-off.

nodes.label: Rebuild goals vs. current WordPress site
nodes.norm_label: rebuild goals vs. current wordpress site
nodes.rationale: Keep brand/categories/dark-blue-and-yellow identity; improve performance, UI/UX clarity, mobile, and distinct audience entry points; drop e-commerce and LMS in v1.

nodes.label: Audience-first homepage design principle
nodes.rationale: Unlike the current WordPress feed, surface distinct per-audience entry points above the general content: hero with bilingual pitch/CTAs and optional admin-managed count-up stats, then students/parents, schools, sponsors blocks, then achievements/news/videos/downloads.

nodes.label: Download center taxonomy (split flat categories)
nodes.rationale: Software and posters were split out of flat DownloadResource because one flat row can't represent 'one app, several platform builds' or per-competition poster categories; datasheets became a two-level part/variant catalog.

nodes.label: Navigation structure recommendation (max 2 levels)
nodes.rationale: Restructure the 5-item deep mega-menu into top-level groups matching audience intent; persistent header CTAs (enroll, language switch, search); sponsors/schools/careers/privacy/terms in footer. Cuts ~5 mega-menus with 8-15 items each to something scannable.

nodes.label: Light and dark mode with pre-paint resolution
nodes.norm_label: light and dark mode with pre-paint resolution
nodes.rationale: Default follows prefers-color-scheme; if unset default to dark. Explicit toggle choice persisted in localStorage (pishnam-theme) overrides system preference; apply as data-theme on html resolved before first paint to avoid a flash of wrong theme.

nodes.label: No public User model in v1
nodes.norm_label: no public user model in v1
nodes.rationale: No accounts, no public auth; visitor interaction is via Lead and Feedback only.

nodes.label: Local-disk media storage (persistent Docker volume)
nodes.rationale: Named volume mounted at /app/uploads or files are lost on every rebuild; nginx serving statically is recommended; back up the volume with Postgres. Paths are plain strings so a later S3/R2/MinIO migration needs no schema change.

nodes.label: Upload security checklist (10 mandatory server-side checks)
nodes.norm_label: upload security checklist (10 mandatory server-side checks)
nodes.rationale: Local disk lacks managed-object-store protections, so: auth first, type allowlist not blocklist, magic-byte verification, re-encode images via jimp, max file size, random filenames, store/serve with no execute permission, rate limit, malware scan if feasible, log every upload. Applies uniformly — public-facing files are the higher-risk case.

nodes.label: Custom admin decision (not Strapi/headless CMS)
nodes.rationale: Content volume is small (dozens of items), solo project with a single-repo requirement, added manually. A separate CMS adds infrastructure, a second auth system, and upgrade overhead not justified at this scale; a custom /admin backed by Prisma is faster to build and simpler to run. Revisit Strapi/Payload if editors or workflows grow.

nodes.label: Definition of done (development guidelines)
nodes.rationale: Both locales, responsive, no console errors, lint/typecheck/tests pass, admin-editable content, metadata per 07, and every item of the upload security checklist re-verified on every PR touching an upload path.

nodes.label: jimp image re-encoding (replaced sharp)
nodes.rationale: sharp's prebuilt binaries need an x86-64-v2 CPU the production host doesn't have; jimp ships no WebP codec (so image/webp is not an accepted upload type), and removing sharp also turns off Next Image Optimization (images.unoptimized in next.config.ts). Uploads are capped at 2400px on the long edge instead.

nodes.label: Parallel xFa/xEn fields vs *Translation tables
nodes.rationale: Rich-text-heavy models (Course, Article) use a separate *Translation table so adding a locale later doesn't mean a schema migration on the parent table; simple models use parallel fields and src/lib/i18n/pick.ts (pickLocaleField).

nodes.label: Upload security checklist (src/lib/upload.ts)
nodes.rationale: Admin-auth-only, allowlisted types, magic-byte content verification (not filename/Content-Type), image re-encoding via jimp, random filenames, no execute permission, rate limiting, and UploadLog audit logging. Not optional hardening to add later — build it in from the first upload endpoint.

nodes.label: CI/CD workflows (ci.yml, deploy.yml)
nodes.rationale: ci.yml runs Prisma migration checks (validate/diff) to catch schema drift; deploy.yml builds app/migrator/seeder images, pushes to GHCR, then SSHes to the VPS to pull and restart (same shape as PishTalk's deploy).

nodes.label: Git conventions (trunk-based, Conventional Commits)
nodes.rationale: Short-lived feature branches, merge to main via PR even solo so CI gates everything, Conventional Commits for scannable history.

nodes.label: ci.yml — PR and push checks
nodes.rationale: No E2E step: @playwright/test is installed and npm run test:e2e exists, but there is no playwright.config.ts and no specs, so the command currently fails; the CI job was removed rather than left permanently red.

nodes.label: deploy.yml — image build, SSH stream, rollout
nodes.norm_label: deploy.yml — image build, ssh stream, rollout
nodes.rationale: Builds web (and migrator only when its inputs changed), docker save, streams to the server over SSH, retags to :current, rolls the stack at /opt/pishnam, then polls /robots.txt through the published port.

nodes.label: Rollback by image retag
nodes.rationale: Every deploy leaves an image tagged with the commit SHA; rolling back is a retag, but it rolls back code only — prisma migrate deploy has no down-migrations.

nodes.label: Right-sized testing strategy (Vitest / RTL / Playwright)
nodes.rationale: Unit tests for zod/utilities/lead-status transitions, component tests for LeadCaptureForm/AdminForm, and a small high-value Playwright smoke suite (homepage both locales, course page, enroll submit, admin login) — not yet written, so the CI job was removed.

nodes.label: NEXT_PUBLIC_* build-time configuration
nodes.rationale: Frozen into the bundle by next build (server-side code included), passed as Docker build args by the deploy workflow rather than read from the server's .env; pointing at a real domain means editing SITE_URL in deploy.yml and redeploying.

nodes.rationale: A trapezoidal lower panel with a horizontal slot reads as either a cassette tape or a card slot forming the robot's mouth; the exact intended object is AMBIGUOUS, but it clearly functions as the face's lower feature.

nodes.label: Red-and-white flag-like crown motif
nodes.rationale: A stepped cap above the face carries white and red bands plus steel blue, echoing the colors of the Iranian flag and suggesting an Iranian robotics club; whether it is meant as a cap or a flag is AMBIGUOUS.

nodes.label: Friendly robot-face mascot
nodes.rationale: A cartoon robot face gives a robotics education club a playful, kid-friendly identity suitable for first-grade learners, while the mechanical panel lines keep it readable as an engineering/robotics emblem for older students and sponsors.

nodes.label: Shield / badge enclosure
nodes.rationale: The rounded shield silhouette frames the mascot as an emblem, reinforcing credibility and achievement signaling used by sponsor, school and competition-results pages.

nodes.norm_label: twin circular eyes on gold faceplate
nodes.rationale: Two large off-white circular pupils inside dark navy rings on a gold faceplate are the logo's primary focal point and the main source of its friendly, approachable character.

nodes.label: Pishnam robot-badge logo
nodes.rationale: The existing Pishnam Robotics Researchers robot-badge logo is kept as-is in the site rebuild to preserve brand continuity; the brand doc explicitly says not to design a new logo and to use only a temporary placeholder until the final production file arrives.
